- `npm run check` fails about twenty tests in a Claude Code session on the maintainer's Mac, in files that spawn processes, send signals or open sockets, with `EPERM`, `EBADF`, `ENOENT` on a stand-in binary, or a five-second timeout, and the same tests fail on a clean `origin/main` there. Cause: the session runs its commands inside Claude Code's own sandbox, which refuses those operations; it is not the load and not the change. A cloud session and CI have no such sandbox. From a host session, run the test files your change touches, say in the report that the whole gate cannot pass there and which files failed on `origin/main` too, and take CI on the exact head as the gate of record. Never read a background command's exit code as the gate's: on [pull request #634](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/634) the coordinator did, and started a round on a head whose gate had failed.

# The three reviews run first on one head

Status: ruled by the maintainer on 2026-11-27, in the coordinator's session. The coordinator proposed it; the maintainer asked for the draft and agreed its text that day.

## Problem

Every pull request gets Codex's adversarial review, a Melian round and the Claude review of record. AGENTS.md ran them one after another: Codex first, then its fixes, then a round, then its fixes, then the review of record. Each reviewer saw different code. A defect Codex found was fixed before Melian's round ran, so the round could neither find it nor miss it.

Example: the maintainer's parity loop needed to know which defects each reviewer finds. For the three pull requests it measured, [#613](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/613), [#619](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/619) and [#623](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/623), the coordinator had to run each reviewer again, blind, on one old head, and build each defect list by hand. About forty pull requests merged between 2026-11-04, the date of the newest comparison record, and 2026-11-27 with all three reviews posted and nothing that could compare them.

## Choice

The three reviews run first on one commit: the first head the builder pushes with its gate green, or with CI green on it where the gate cannot run. The builder starts all three together, pushes no fix until all three have reported, and names the commit in its report as the first reviewed head.

After that head, each fix pass gets a Melian round and nothing else. Codex's review and the review of record run once, on the first reviewed head. The maintainer ruled this on 2026-11-28, in the coordinator's session: "we've reached a level of recall that I'm satisfied with only using All 3 models for that first code review to build up our parity database. Following fixes, lets just use the melian review." The cost is accepted: no reviewer but Melian reads a fix commit, where Codex's review used to run after each fix pass and the review of [cut at 2 KiB]

Choice: the builder of a pull request runs Codex's adversarial review on its own branch, and its own Melian rounds through the `melian round` workflow, before the first round and after each fix pass. It posts the review's JSON and its findings in the pull request's report, and fixes from them. The coordinator still reads the verdicts, runs the round a dismissal or the comparison record needs, marks the pull request ready and queues it.

explanation.what: The new decision narrows an active decision without declaring it. [Builders run Codex's adversarial review and their own Melian rounds](docs/decisions/2026-11-05-builders-run-their-own-reviews.md) chooses that the builder runs Codex's review "before the first round and after each fix pass". Line 15 of the new decision overrides that clause: Codex's review runs once, on the first reviewed head. The file has no `Amends:` line for the 2026-11-05 decision.
explanation.whatToDo: Add `Amends: [Builders run Codex's adversarial review and their own Melian rounds](2026-11-05-builders-run-their-own-reviews.md), when Codex's review runs` near the top of the new decision file.
explanation.whyHere: AGENTS.md's "Lessons live here" section says: "For a narrow change, add `Amends: <target link>, <scope>` (the scope is optional), one declaration per line; the target stays active and the amendment wins where they conflict." Without that declaration, the decision index presents both files as active and equal, and they contradict each other on when Codex's review runs.

properties.failureScenario: Step 26's supersession check builds the decision graph from `Amends:` and `Supersedes:` lines. With no edge from this file to the 2026-11-05 decision, both stay active and neither wins. The 2026-11-05 decision still tells a builder to run Codex's review \"after each fix pass\", and the design lens's `contradicts-documented-decision` rule reads it as current policy. A builder or lens that consults the index gets two active decisions that disagree, and nothing says the newer one wins.
